title: Construction of DAG Models for Autonomous Systems
problem: Constructing optimal directed acyclic graph (DAG) task models for autonomous systems (vehicles, drones) to minimize end-to-end response time, particularly for time-triggered blended task chains.
motivation: DAG scheduling has been extensively studied, but construction of the DAG model itself is rarely addressed; better model topology can significantly reduce system response time and improve autonomous system performance.
method: Proposes representation semantics for time-triggered task chains in autonomous systems and introduces a topology optimization method that improves average end-to-end response time by 4.8x compared to Floyd algorithm with O(n²) complexity suitable for dynamic task handling.
key_novelty: First systematic study of DAG model construction (rather than scheduling) with focus on time-triggered autonomous system task chains and associated topology optimization method.
contributions: Addresses the understudied problem of DAG model construction in autonomous systems
Proposes representation semantics for time-triggered blended task chains
Develops topology optimization method achieving 4.8x response time reduction over Floyd algorithm
O(n²) complexity enabling handling of dynamic tasks

metrics.speedup: 4.8x end-to-end response time reduction vs. Floyd algorithm

primary_theme: DAG model construction for autonomous system task scheduling
